findings.evidence: the symlink fix guards only the destination leaf: `+        if dest.is_symlink():` / `+            raise OnboardError(` / `+                f"destination is a symlink — refusing to install {rel} "` — while the write path below it is unchanged (`dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` + write_bytes per the round-1 record). A hostile target tree carrying a SYMLINKED PARENT directory (e.g. `factory -> /outside/dir`) defeats the guard: `dest.is_symlink()` is False for `factory/KICKOFF.md` when only the parent is a link, mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) passes through the link to an existing outside directory, and the write lands outside the target. The round-1 required change was explicit: 'refuse ... when dest OR ANY COMPONENT OF dest.parent inside the target is a symlink, or resolve dest and verify it stays within target.resolve(); apply the same check to the mkdir(parents=True) path'. All three shipped tests (TestInstallerSymlinkGuard in onboarding/tests/test_onboard.py) plant the symlink at the destination file only, so moving the link one level up to a parent directory leaves the suite green while the escape works — the fix is incomplete against its own required change.
findings.required_change: extend the install_bytes guard to the full destination path: refuse (named OnboardError) when any component of dest from the target root down — including dest.parent directories created or traversed by mkdir(parents=True) — is a symlink, or resolve dest and verify resolved.is_relative_to(self.target.resolve()) before any write; add a test planting the symlink at a PARENT directory (e.g. factory -> outside) asserting the refusal and that nothing is written outside.

findings.evidence: the issue-form classification fix stays substring-based: `+        if "404" in detail and "not found" in detail.lower():` / `             return {"present": False, "path": None}` — the round-1 required change was to 'match the HTTP status structurally (e.g. the leading `HTTP 404` of gh api's error output ...) instead of an unanchored "404" substring'. Conjoining a second unanchored token narrows the misclassification class (the shipped tests pin that `pipeline 4041 failed` and `HTTP 404: API rate limit exceeded` are now named ProbeErrors) but does not eliminate it: any unrelated failure whose stderr happens to carry both tokens anywhere — an intercepting proxy's `404 ... Not Found` error page, an error quoting a URL or repo path containing `404` plus a `not found` phrase — is still silently reclassified as genuine template absence instead of a named probe failure, so a transport-level error is reported downstream as a legitimate 'form absent' result.
findings.required_change: anchor the absence classification to the gh api error grammar (e.g. require detail to start with `HTTP 404` / match `^HTTP 404\b` case-insensitively) and raise the named ProbeError for every other non-zero-rc stderr; add a stubbed-transport test for a both-tokens-present but unanchored error body (e.g. a proxy page quoting `404` mid-text with `not found`) asserting the named refusal.
